sources.phase_takeaway: Future connector and MCP work should preserve explicit authorization boundaries and reject token passthrough assumptions.
Multi-agent runners should treat tool use, identity, memory, inter-agent communication, and cascading failure as first-class risk surfaces.
AI-factory planning should emphasize agent throughput, context-memory protection, and infrastructure-level security rather than abstract scale claims.
Simulation and OS planning should track confidential compute, interconnect scale, and GPU fabric boundaries as implementation constraints.

sources.phase_takeaway: Agent deployment patterns should separate local orchestration receipts from managed-agent runtime assumptions.

runner_implications: Add explicit identity, memory, and inter-agent communication checks to future runner inventories.
Keep watcher receipts status-only and avoid token, path, or raw transport leakage.
Treat connector write actions as separate approvals, not automatic extensions of read/search workflows.
Keep GMUT/THOS infrastructure synthesis grounded in verifiable platform constraints.
